Article Title: Apple Mac minis and Mac Studios have disappeared from store shelves in many countries, and how this shortage links to OpenAI and Anthropic
Article Text:
OpenAI reportedly bought tens of thousands of Apple Macs for AI

Why Mac mini and Mac Studio are attracting AI developers

OpenClaw craze adds to Mac mini demand in China

Apple’s Mac mini and Mac Studio computers have become increasingly difficult to find in several markets, and the AI boom may be playing a surprising role in the shortage. According to a report by The information, OpenAI has bought tens of thousands of Mac minis and Mac Studios for work involving AI agents and reinforcement learning, while Anthropic has reportedly rented Mac minis through Amazon Web Services for similar tasks. At the same time, developers and consumers are increasingly turning to Apple's compact computers to run AI agents locally. The demand has been particularly visible in China, where the popularity of OpenClaw has reportedly pushed Mac mini stocks down and prices up.According to The Information, OpenAI has spent several months buying tens of thousands of Mac minis and Mac Studios. The computers are reportedly being used for reinforcement learning and AI agents that can interact with computers.Anthropic has also reportedly been using Mac minis, although through a different route. The Claude maker is said to have rented the machines through Amazon Web Services for similar AI work.The demand highlights an unusual role for Apple's small desktop computers. Macs are not replacing Nvidia's powerful GPUs for training the largest AI models. Instead, they can be useful for another growing area of artificial intelligence: AI agents that interact with regular computer environments.Such agents can look at a screen, use a browser, click buttons and repeatedly attempt tasks. Running many such sessions can require a large number of computers.One reason is Apple's unified memory architecture. Instead of keeping CPU and GPU memory completely separate, Apple silicon allows different parts of the system to access a common pool of memory. High-memory Mac configurations can therefore run some local AI models that may struggle to fit within the dedicated memory available on consumer graphics cards.The machines also offer developers a complete macOS environment. That can matter when an AI agent needs to learn how to operate software and perform tasks on a desktop rather than simply process information in a data centre.Demand is not limited to large AI companies. The Mac mini has also become a popular choice among people running OpenClaw, an open-source AI agent. The trend has been particularly visible in China, where running OpenClaw has become known as “raising a lobster”, a reference to the project's mascot.According to the South China Morning Post, Mac minis were selling out at retailers in parts of China earlier this year. Some sellers with remaining stock were reportedly charging hundreds of yuan above normal prices.The Mac mini's appeal for OpenClaw is also linked to security. AI agents can require extensive permissions to control a computer, access information and carry out tasks. Running such software on a person's main computer could create risks if permissions are incorrectly configured or third-party tools contain malicious code.That has encouraged some users to run AI agents on a separate machine. The Mac mini's small size and ability to run AI workloads locally have made it one option for such setups.
Article Summary: OpenAI reportedly bought tens of thousands of Apple Macs for AI. The computers are reportedly being used for reinforcement learning and AI agents that can interact with computers. The Mac mini has also become a popular choice among people running OpenClaw, an open-source AI agent.

Article Title: Sony Music and Warner Chappell Music sue Anthropic; lawsuit that names Dario Amodei accuse Anthropic of 'illegally torrenting, scraping, and downloading' copyrighted songs to train Claude
Article Text:
Sony Music and Warner Chappell accuse Anthropic of copyright infringement

Anthropic faces scrutiny over how it gets training data

What Anthropic says

Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell Music have sued Anthropic, accusing the AI company of using copyrighted songs without permission to train its Claude models. The lawsuit, filed in a Northern California federal court last week, also names Anthropic co-founders Dario Amodei and Benjamin Mann. The music publishers allege that Anthropic engaged in “illegally torrenting, scraping, and downloading” copyrighted songs, including works such as “Eye of the Tiger,” Marvin Gaye’s “Ain’t No Mountain High Enough” and Taylor Swift’s “Paper Rings.” The case adds another major copyright fight to the growing legal battle between AI companies and rights holders over how copyrighted material can be used to train AI systems.The lawsuit claims Anthropic obtained copyrighted music and used it in the development and training of Claude. Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell Music are seeking a jury trial and statutory damages of up to $150,000 for each infringed composition.The publishers also allege that Claude can reproduce copyrighted song lyrics in its responses. They argue that this could allow users to obtain lyrics through the AI chatbot instead of using licensed lyric services, potentially hurting the market for music publishers and songwriters.The complaint names several well-known songs as examples of works allegedly involved in the case.The latest lawsuit comes after Anthropic faced a major copyright case involving books. In June 2025, a court found that Anthropic had downloaded more than 7 million pirated books from sources including Library Genesis and Pirate Library Mirror. The judge found that Anthropic's use of copyrighted books to train its AI models qualified as fair use, but the acquisition of pirated copies remained a separate issue.That dispute was later resolved through a $1.5 billion settlement.Anthropic has rejected the claims made by the music publishers. “We disagree with the publishers’ claims and we intend to defend ourselves robustly in court,” an Anthropic spokesperson said, according to Benzinga.The lawsuit is also not Anthropic's first legal fight over copyrighted music. In a separate case filed in 2023, Universal Music Group, Concord Music Group and ABKCO sued Anthropic over the alleged use and reproduction of copyrighted song lyrics.
Article Summary: Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell Music accuse Anthropic of copyright infringement. The music publishers allege that Anthropic engaged in “illegally torrenting, scraping, and downloading” copyrighted songs. The case adds another major copyright fight to the growing legal battle between AI companies and rights holders over how copyrighted material can be used to train AI systems.

Article Title: On his last day as Apple CEO, Tim Cook sends memo to employees; says: I am not leaving Apple, but I am...
Article Text:
Tim Cook signs off as Apple CEO after 15 years, hands over to John Ternus.

Tim Cook hands Apple to John Ternus, a hardware man and not a services one

Tim Cook is not leaving Apple, he is changing desks

Here's Tim Cook's final memo to Apple employees, in full

Team,

Today is my last day as CEO of Apple. This is a moment I always knew would come one day, and yet it is still hard to believe it has arrived and I am writing these words.

I love this company and the team behind it, and I couldn’t let this day pass without sending a note to you to tell you how grateful I am for the outpouring of affection you’ve sent my way, for the way you’ve shown up each and every day, and most of all, for the privilege of a lifetime serving as your leader.

The truth is, whatever there is to say about my success, I know it is all because of you. You have brought out the best in me. In all my life, I have never seen or been with such an extraordinary team of people before, and every day I get to see more examples of that.

There is something truly special about Apple. I am most proud of what an annual report could never capture. This place is proof that culture triumphs over everything. We share a belief that what we build matters and that we have both the opportunity and the responsibility to leave the world better than we found it. That purpose is part of what makes this place extraordinary. Apple helps nurture it, but I believe it lived within each of you long before you arrived here.

It is what brought you to this company and what continues to drive the work you do every day.

Together, we have created something far greater than any one of us could have imagined or accomplished alone. And that’s the secret to our success. We bring out the best in each other. We lift each other up. We have made it possible to leave our “dent in the universe,” as Steve once described it, because of who we are and what we believe, because of what we value and how we see the world.

How fortunate we are. How fortunate I am.

As you know, I am not leaving Apple. But I am stepping away from a role that I have loved deeply. I will miss this work in ways I can only begin to imagine, even as I remain completely at peace with my decision. I will miss leading you and being with you for every step, even as I take enormous comfort in handing the helm to someone as brilliant and wonderful and capable as John. Few people understand what it takes to build products that change the world the way John does and I could not be more excited for his leadership.

I hope you know how much I appreciate you and what an honor it has been to be your CEO. Most of all, I hope you will continue to be proud to be part of this remarkable place we call Apple and always give it your very best. When we bring our whole selves to this work, with care for one another and for the people we serve, there is no limit to the profound difference we can make.

I look forward to seeing you in my new role at Apple Park and around the world.

With all I have and all I am, I am always.

Yours,

Tim

Tim Cook signed off as Apple chief executive on Monday the way he ran the company for 15 years, calmly and with the credit pushed elsewhere. In a farewell memo to Apple employees on his final day in the job, Cook wrote that this was a moment he always knew would come, and that it was still hard to believe he was writing the words. John Ternus takes over as Apple CEO on September 1.The Tim Cook memo is notable for what it leaves out. There is no product tease, no roadmap, and no mention of AI, regulation or China, the three pressures that will shape Ternus's first year. Instead Cook spends most of it thanking staff, arguing that Apple's culture is the thing an annual report can never capture, and reaching back to Steve Jobs and his line about leaving a dent in the universe. The sentence employees were waiting for came late. He is not leaving Apple, he said, only stepping away from a role he has loved deeply.Cook saved his warmest paragraph for his successor. He called Ternus brilliant and capable, and said few people understand what it takes to build world-changing products the way Ternus does. Coming from a CEO long accused of running Apple like an operations manager, the choice of words is pointed.Ternus has been senior vice president of hardware engineering, overseeing the entire device line-up.Recent launches under him include the ultra-thin iPhone Air, the cheaper MacBook Neo, and AirPods with hearing health features. Apple also pulled its Mac mini and Mac Studio releases earlier in the year to meet AI-driven demand. The promotion reads as a bet on hardware execution rather than a pivot to services.From Tuesday, Cook becomes executive chairman of Apple's board. He keeps the portfolio he was best at, managing governments in Washington and Beijing, at a point when tariff demands and political requests are landing on Apple's desk with some regularity.Cook took over from Jobs in August 2011. The 15 years since brought the Apple Watch, AirPods, and a vastly expanded iPhone, iPad and Mac business. On X, he told the Apple community that his title changes on Tuesday but his affection for them will not, and signed the memo: "With all I have and all I am, I am always. Yours, Tim."
Article Summary: Tim Cook signs off as Apple CEO after 15 years, hands over to John Ternus. Tim Cook memo is notable for what it leaves out. There is no product tease, no roadmap, and no mention of AI, regulation or China. Cook spends most of it thanking staff, arguing that Apple's culture is the most important thing.

Article Title: Chinese chipmaker that sued Pentagon makes breakthrough in memory chips
Article Text:
CXMT is China's leading producer of dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) chips.

CXMT latest memory hardware attracts big Chinese players

Chinese memory chipmaker ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) has reportedly made a breakthrough in advanced memory chips even as the tech industry is witnessing unprecedented demand for RAMs. As per a report by The Information (via news agency Reuters), the company has started manufacturing advanced high-bandwidth memory (HBM) in limited volumes. Citing two people familiar with the development, the report revealed that CXMT is producing HBM3E, an advanced class of high-bandwidth memory silicon essential for powering artificial intelligence (AI) hardware.The semiconductor manufacturer aims to ramp up larger-scale mass production by 2027, the report added. Multiple domestic semiconductor design firms are already evaluating CXMT’s latest memory hardware to integrate with their proprietary computing silicon.Prominent Chinese tech players, including Alibaba Group’s chip-design division T-Head and Beijing-based Cambricon Technologies, are said to be actively testing the HBM3E components alongside their in-house AI processors.If ongoing qualification testing succeeds, these technology firms plan to integrate CXMT's memory modules into commercial products as early as next year, the report pointed out.Recently, China's largest memory chipmaker sued the Pentagon after the company was placed on a list of companies the US government says support China's military. The lawsuit marks the latest escalation between Beijing's tech sector and Washington over trade restrictions tied to national security concerns.“CXMT is not affiliated with the Chinese military. CXMT designs, produces, and sells its DRAM chips for civilian and commercial use, not for military use,” the company said in its federal lawsuit. The US Defense Department declined to comment on the specifics of the case, saying, “As a matter of policy, the Department does not comment on pending or ongoing litigation.”CXMT has also recently drawn attention after Apple reportedly made a special request to US officials regarding its status. The Cupertino-based tech giant has also reportedly held early talks with CXMT for iPhones and MacBooks which will be sold within the Chinese market.
Article Summary: ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) has reportedly made a breakthrough in advanced memory chips. The company has started manufacturing advanced high- bandwidth memory (HBM) in limited volumes. Multiple domestic semiconductor design firms are already evaluating CXMT’s latest memory hardware to integrate with their proprietary computing silicon.

Article Title: In 2025, researchers used fired clay bricks and eggshell waste, reducing energy consumption for heating and cooling by 50%, turning food waste into useful building material
Article Text:
AI generated Image for representational purpose

How eggshell waste was added to clay bricks

10% eggshell bricks showed the biggest drop in heat transfer

The waste problem is part of the attraction

A pile of discarded eggshells could have a surprising second life: inside building bricks. In 2025, researchers in Egypt tested fired clay bricks made with eggshell waste. As part of the study, researchers then found that the right amount of eggshell powder can significantly reduce heat transfer through the material. The study found that bricks containing 10% eggshell waste and fired at 1,100°C recorded a 50% reduction in thermal conductivity compared with ordinary clay bricks. Researchers also found that the thermal diffusivity and thermal effusivity also fell by about 30%.The researchers collected eggshells, cleaned and dried them, then ground them into powder. The powder was mixed with clay from Egypt's Kharga Oasis. Researchers used different proportions of eggshells ranging from 1% to 10%.The study found that eggshells changed the internal structure of the bricks. During high-temperature firing, calcium carbonate in the eggshells breaks down and releases carbon dioxide. This process helps create pores inside the material.The strongest thermal result came from the brick containing 10% eggshell waste. Compared to the untreated clay brick, the researchers recorded a 50% drop in thermal conductivity, meaning less heat could pass through the material.Thermal diffusivity and thermal effusivity each fell by about 30%, the research found.The results, researchers believe, can have significance for buildings in hot climates, where walls absorb and transfer heat from the outside into indoor spaces. Bricks with more air spaces can slow heat movement because air is a poor conductor of heat. The researchers found that adding eggshell waste changed the brick's internal structure and density, creating conditions that improved its insulation performance.The study also points to another potential benefit: recycling eggshells instead of sending them to landfills. The researchers noted that more than 110 billion eggshells are estimated to end up in landfills worldwide. Turning some of this waste into construction material could give it a useful purpose while reducing the need for some raw materials.
Article Summary: Researchers in Egypt tested fired clay bricks made with eggshell waste. Found that the right amount of eggshell powder can significantly reduce heat transfer through the material. Researchers collected eggshells, cleaned and dried them, then ground them into powder. powder was mixed with clay from Egypt's Kharga Oasis.

Article Title: California passes bill that won't require Linux and other open-source systems to follow the state's age verification law
Article Text:
Representative Image

How the amendment redefines who the law covers

"operating system provider"

"under license terms that permit a recipient to copy, redistribute, and modify the software."

"offered to consumers as a stand-alone executable application through a covered application store"

Fixing a definition that classified every adult as a child

"user,"

"a child that is the primary user of a device,"

What remains covered, and what's not still unclear

California's legislature has passed Assembly Bill 1856, exempting open-source operating systems from the state's Digital Age Assurance Act. The move comes months before the law is due to take effect on January 1, 2027. The California Senate amended and passed the bill this month in a 39-0 vote, and the Assembly accepted the changes in a concurrence vote soon after. The amendment ends almost a year of uncertainty surrounding whether Linux distributions and SteamOS would be forced to collect user age data during account setup alongside Windows, macOS, iOS and Android. AB 1856 has now been sent to Governor Gavin Newsom, who signed the original act into law last October.The amendments redefine the termto exclude any person or entity that distributes an OS or applicationAny software distributed under the GPL, MIT, BSD and Apache licenses satisfies that test, which removes the likes of Debian, Fedora, Ubuntu, Arch and the BSD family from AB 1856's scope.A second exclusion removes software components that aren'tfrom the law's definition of an application, covering libraries and dependencies distributed through package managers like apt and pacman.AB 1856 doesn't explicitly say that repos aren't app stores, but a store's main obligation under the law is to request an age signal from the user's OS provider and pass it to developers; an exempt open-source OS produces no signal.A third carve-out excludes storefronts distributing extensions or add-ons that run exclusively inside a host application, which takes browser extension stores out of scope.The amendments to AB 1856 also remove the original definition ofwhich read,and technically classified every device owner in California as a child.The law's signalling framework depends on adults declaring their age on account setup, so their devices get flagged as 18 and over, but under that definition nobody could ever be flagged as an adult. Left uncorrected, that wording would have undermined the entire mechanism the law relies on to distinguish adult users from minors.Lawmakers also inserted a new provision prohibiting anyone from requesting an age signal from an OS provider or app store unless required by law. That closes off potential abuse of the age API that could have led to it being used as a general-purpose data collection channel even when age verification wasn't required. Platforms and developers also gain a good-faith safe harbour against erroneous signals, protecting them from liability when age-gating signals are inaccurate.Windows, macOS, iOS and Android remain fully in scope, with age collection required at account setup from January 1, 2027. A later July 1, 2027 deadline applies to devices set up before January 1.Whether SteamOS is in scope isn't yet clear. Its Arch-based system components are open source, but Valve distributes the image alongside the proprietary Steam client, leaving its status under the amended law ambiguous.GrapheneOS, which in March said it would refuse to comply with age-verification mandates, is distributed under the open-source MIT and Apache licenses and now falls outside the law's scope entirely, though Brazil's Digital ECA still applies.Assembly member Buffy Wicks, who wrote both the Digital Age Assurance Act and the AB 1856 amendment, introduced the exemption back in February following criticism from Linux developers and the Electronic Frontier Foundation.
Article Summary: California legislature passes bill exempting open-source operating systems from Digital Age Assurance Act. The move comes months before the law is due to take effect on January 1, 2027. The amendment ends almost a year of uncertainty surrounding whether Linux distributions and SteamOS would be forced to collect user age data.

Article Title: In 2024, Netflix told shareholders it needed no partners; now its co-CEO Greg Peters says outside deals are ‘very promising’
Article Text:
Netflix co-CEO Greg Peters

"already operates as a go-to destination for entertainment.”

"very promising,"

"If we see additional deals that similarly serve our members, that work for our partner, that work for us, we'll certainly consider them,"

Netflix shifts its tone on partnerships

Other streaming giants are also racing to bundle

"The thing that matters is that when you turn on the TV, what app are you opening for the next three hours?"

Two years ago, Netflix told its shareholders that the companyThis made it clear that the streaming giant saw little need to feature rival services within its own app. Now, that position has softened considerably. Speaking on its latest earnings call, Netflix co-chief executive Greg Peters described the early results of a new partnership with French broadcaster TF1 asand signalled the company is open to striking similar deals elsewhere.Peters said.Netflix's moves have been more subtle than some of its rivals, but that could soon change. In June, the company began streaming TF1 in its French markets, including a live feed of TF1 networks and on-demand programs. It marked Netflix's first arrangement of its kind, and it appears to be a test case for something larger.A report by The New York Times cited three people familiar with the discussions, who said Netflix executives recently held talks with NBCUniversal and the Fox Corporation about bringing Peacock and Fox One to Netflix's platform.However, the people warned that no deal is imminent, and that it remains unclear whether Netflix would absorb the outside content directly into its own service, as in a recent YouTube-Peacock arrangement, or instead act more as a retailer, similar to how Amazon Prime Video operates.Netflix is not alone in this pivot. For years, Amazon has persuaded tens of millions of people to use its Prime Video app to subscribe to other services, like HBO Max or Apple TV, and to watch shows like "The Pitt" or "Ted Lasso" from within the retail giant's digital walls. Now, other streaming leaders are sprinting to catch up.YouTube and Roku are racing to become one-stop shops for all the content people watch on their televisions. People who pay for a commercial-free YouTube tier, for example, will soon have access to Peacock content like "The Traitors" and "Sunday Night Football" as part of a recent deal between the two companies.The push underscores a broader competitive shift among the titans of streaming television. Companies that were once laser-focused on gaining new subscribers are now far more concerned with keeping those people watching as much as possible, and cancelling as little as possible. What were once described as the streaming wars have effectively morphed into bundling wars. The biggest streaming firms are no longer content to just have the most subscribers; they also want to be the main entry point to everything streaming has to offer.Jonathan Carson, chief executive of Antenna, a subscription research firm, told the NYT.Consumers already appear receptive to managing their subscriptions through a single platform. Over the last three years, subscriptions made via third-party platforms like Amazon, Roku or YouTube have grown roughly 60 per cent, according to Antenna, with about a third of all new subscriptions now purchased this way.
Article Summary: Netflix's new partnership with French broadcaster TF1 is "very promising," says co-CEO Greg Peters. The company has also held talks with NBCUniversal and the Fox Corporation about bringing Peacock and Fox One to Netflix's platform. The push underscores a broader competitive shift among the titans of streaming television.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Peter Thiel: People are spending way too much time thinking about climate change, way too little thinking about AI

What Peter Thiel's quote implies

Peter Thiel's background and views on technology

Billionaire investor and entrepreneur Peter Thiel has weighed in on how society is allocating its attention between two major issues of the era. He said:The statement reflects Thiel's longstanding focus on artificial intelligence as a defining technological and economic force, one he has argued deserves more public and institutional attention than it currently receives. The comparison to climate change, a topic that has occupied significant space in policy debates, media coverage and public consciousness for decades, frames Thiel's point as one about relative priorities rather than an outright rejection of climate concerns.Peter Thiel is a German-born American entrepreneur and investor who co-founded PayPal in the late 1990s before it was sold to eBay in 2002. He later co-founded Palantir Technologies, a data analytics company, and became an early outside investor in Facebook.Thiel has also been a general partner at Founders Fund, a venture capital firm that has backed numerous technology companies.Beyond his business ventures, Thiel has been an outspoken commentator on technology, innovation and the pace of scientific progress, often arguing that society has grown complacent in pursuing major technological breakthroughs. His views on artificial intelligence fit within that broader pattern of commentary, positioning AI as a subject that, in his assessment, has not received attention proportionate to its significance.

Article Title: Google, Microsoft and Apple's 'European troubles' now also become of OpenAI, Roblox and Reddit, as Europe cannot stop…
Article Text:
The EU has decided a chatbot that searches the web is a search engine

Compliance under the Digital Services Act means audits, risk reports and open data

The European Commission has added ChatGPT to the small club of online services it polices most closely, making OpenAI 's chatbot the first AI assistant to fall under the strictest tier of the Digital Services Act. In the same decision on Monday, Brussels designated Reddit and Roblox as Very Large Online Platforms. The compliance headaches that Google , Microsoft and Apple have spent years managing in Europe now belong to three more American companies.ChatGPT has been classified as a Very Large Online Search Engine rather than a platform, and that is the part worth paying attention to. The Commission decided that a chatbot answering prompts by pulling live results off the web is doing a search engine's job, whatever the interface looks like. The three services have four months, until January 2027, to comply. The penalty ceiling for failing is six per cent of global annual turnover.The threshold for this tier is 45 million average monthly users in the EU, about one in ten people in the bloc. ChatGPT's search function reported roughly 159 million monthly users for the six months ending March 2026. Reddit declared 57.2 million and Roblox 46.6 million, which puts the gaming platform barely over the line.Companies self-declare these numbers, and all three did.EU tech chief Henna Virkkunen said the three services would now be held to a "higher standard of scrutiny and accountability", in line with their impact on citizens. The DSA's strictest tier now covers 28 platforms and search engines.The work ahead is unglamorous. Each service must run annual systemic risk assessments covering illegal content, harm to minors, users' physical and mental wellbeing, fundamental rights, elections and public security. They must also open themselves to independent audits and share data with regulators and vetted researchers. Ireland's Coimisiún na Meán will supervise ChatGPT and Reddit, while the Dutch consumer authority takes Roblox.OpenAI said it accepts that ChatGPT search operates as a search service under the DSA and is preparing for the extra requirements. Roblox called itself the first gaming platform to hit the milestone in the EU. Reddit did not comment.Brussels has already collected roughly 870 million euros in DSA fines, including 550 million from AliExpress in July and 120 million from X in December. Washington has called such penalties economic extortion and threatened retaliation. That argument is about to get louder, because the DSA has now reached generative AI, and the list of US companies with European troubles is three names longer.
Article Summary: ChatGPT is the first AI assistant to fall under the strictest tier of the Digital Services Act. The three services have four months, until January 2027, to comply. The penalty ceiling for failing is six per cent of global annual turnover.

Article Title: China and Netherlands continue to fight on chip giant Nexperia, now Chinese court freezes $300 million of company's assets
Article Text:
Chinese court freezes $300 million of Nexperia assets as Wingtech fight drags on

The lawsuit behind the asset freeze is asking for far more than $300 million

How a Dutch national security intervention became a Chinese courtroom fight

A Chinese court has frozen up to 2.14 billion yuan, roughly $300 million, in assets belonging to Dutch chipmaker Nexperia and its equipment arm, handing the company's estranged Chinese owner fresh leverage in a dispute that has now run for close to a year. The order came from the Dongguan Intermediate People's Court and was disclosed by Wingtech Technology in a stock exchange filing, according to Reuters.The freeze covers Nexperia's stakes in four China-based businesses, including its semiconductor operations in China, Wuxi and Shanghai, plus the wholly owned Wuxi unit of its equipment arm. The measures took effect between August 20 and August 25 and stay in place until August 2029. The case has not gone to trial. On paper little has shifted: the board is unchanged and the ownership question is still open. What Wingtech has gained is pressure.Wingtech and a subsidiary filed suit in May, naming Nexperia, its equipment arm, the parent company and three executives. They are seeking 8 billion yuan in damages, arguing the defendants carried out or helped carry out discriminatory Dutch restrictions, and are leaning on China's Anti-Foreign Sanctions Law to make the case.Nexperia and its equipment arm did not immediately respond to requests for comment.This began last year when the Dutch government intervened at Nexperia over concerns that technology, funds and production assets could be moved abroad. The Enterprise Chamber suspended chief executive Zhang Xuezheng and placed the voting rights tied to Wingtech's shareholding under independent management. Beijing answered with export controls on Nexperia's China operations, which disrupted shipments of the cheap, unglamorous chips that cars and consumer electronics run on. Talks between Beijing and The Hague restored the flow of supply and the Netherlands suspended its order, but Wingtech never recovered its voting control.The split has already reshaped how the company makes chips. Nexperia's China unit, cut off from European wafers, said last week it is moving its entire product line to a domestic 12-inch wafer foundry supplied by an unnamed Chinese partner, shifting away from the 8-inch and 6-inch lines it ran before. Diodes, MOSFETs and logic ICs are all part of that move. China accounts for about 70 per cent of Nexperia's output.The freeze runs until August 2029 and the case has not been heard yet, so this could sit unresolved for years. By the time anyone wins the ownership argument, they may be inheriting two companies instead of one.
Article Summary: Wingtech Technology filed suit in May, naming Nexperia, its equipment arm, the parent company and three executives. They are seeking 8 billion yuan in damages, arguing the defendants carried out or helped carry out discriminatory Dutch restrictions. The freeze runs until August 2029 and the case has not been heard yet.

Article Title: PhonePe’s new UPI service lets feature phone users make payments without internet: Here’s how to use the feature
Article Text: PhonePe today announced the launch of PhonePe UPI 123Pay, enabling UPI payment capabilities for feature phone users across India without requiring an internet connection. With this, PhonePe becomes the first major third-party application provider (TPAP) to extend UPI payments to India’s 200 million+ feature phone users, advancing financial inclusion and bringing underserved communities into the digital payments fold.The service will come pre-bundled on devices from Nokia, HMD, Lava International, and Itel Mobile – Transsion Holdings, with additional handset manufacturer partnerships to follow in the coming months. Users can access the service directly on their feature phones, with upcoming updates introducing bill payments, recharges, and Aadhaar-based onboarding.PhonePe UPI 123Pay is built on a robust SMS-based architecture, ensuring reliable transactions even in regions with limited 2G connectivity. Key features include:* Peer-to-peer transfers via mobile numbers or UPI IDs* Peer-to-merchant payments through UPI IDs and QR code scanning* Account management, balance checks, and transaction history* Voice-first AI-powered helpline supporting English and 12 Indian languages for step-by-step activation guidanceRegistration is simple: open the pre-installed PhonePe app, accept terms, select your bank, enter debit card details, set a UPI PIN, and begin making payments immediately.Speaking on the launch, Sameer Nigam, founder and CEO, PhonePe, said: “Bringing UPI to feature phones through PhonePe UPI 123Pay extends the benefits of digital payments beyond smartphones to every corner of the country. To us, this is what building for India actually means—meeting people where they are to drive a truly universal wave of financial inclusion that will onboard the next 300 million users into the digital financial fold. ”
Article Summary: PhonePe launches PhonePe UPI 123Pay, enabling UPI payment capabilities for feature phone users across India. The service will come pre-bundled on devices from Nokia, HMD, Lava International, and Itel Mobile – Transsion Holdings. Users can access the service directly on their feature phones.

Meta's AI-powered smart glasses have run into a growing privacy controversy, as clips of wearers covertly filming women and strangers have spread across social media. Article Summary: Meta's smart glasses have run into a growing privacy controversy. Clips of wearers covertly filming women and strangers have spread across social media. Meta has moved to publicise new privacy settings for its glasses and has launched a public relations push to explain how the hardware works.

Article Title: Fireflies AI co-founder and CEO Krish Ramineni shares the ‘biggest problem’ with Google, Microsoft meeting assistants and how he aims to beat them
Article Text:
Fireflies AI co-founder and CEO Krish Ramineni

Google, Microsoft have ‘closed ecosystem’ problem

Shift from notetaker to ‘action-taker’ and India-centric features

'Fireflies keeping the highest bar in security and privacy'

When tech giants like Google and Microsoft roll out built-in AI features, the immediate reaction of many users is often to write off independent AI startups. This is the billion-dollar question every founder faces. But for Fireflies.ai co-founder and CEO Krish Ramineni, what these tech titans view as their greatest strength is exactly where agile startups are finding their ultimate competitive advantage. The US-based company is betting on cross-platform flexibility, deeper workflow integrations and several India-first features to stay ahead of the competition.Talking with The Times of India tech, Ramineni addressed the long-standing challenge of competing against Silicon Valley's tech giants, highlighting that ecosystem fragmentation remains the single biggest flaw in Big Tech's meeting assistants. While proprietary AI solutions from Google or Microsoft are locked into their own environments, modern professionals and their external clients operate across a scattered mix of calling tools throughout the workday.“This is something that I [have been] thinking about every night for the last five years, even before we really took off. There’s a multi-pronged approach to this one. The simple answer is: knowledge is fragmented.If you're using Google's AI, it’s only going to work on Google and not on [Microsoft] Teams, or Zoom,” Ramineni told TOI.“So, fragmentation is actually something that we can address where you have one AI that works across all platforms and people want consistency,” he added, explaining that employees may have a zoom meeting now; then an hour later, you have a meeting on Teams. And then, a Google Meet meeting.“You need one platform that brings it together. Also, the AI that you use or the video conferencing tools that you use might be different from what your clients or your customers use. So that alone makes it a very compelling value proposition for why people are using Fireflies.ai and continue to use it,” he explained.He further noted that the team has had a lot of time to make the core experience better for a lot of larger companies. “We have to go 10 layers deeper on the quality of the product. We can't just say, ‘Okay, it's good enough to bundle it’. We have to prove our metal every day”, he said, pointing out that the platform now has over 120 different integrations and a rich API that makes it accessible for people.Fireflies is actively expanding into a multi-product company designed to handle broader knowledge work before, during and after meetings. Earlier this month, the company expanded its features by launching an email assistant.With this, the platform is evolving from passive transcription to executing follow-up tasks, such as creating presentation slide decks, drafting post-call emails, building project memos, and pinging colleagues on Slack.Over the coming year, Fireflies plans to introduce roughly a dozen new capabilities outside standard meeting notes, including autonomous voice agents designed to attend and conduct preliminary screening interviews on a user's behalf.When talking about India-centric features, Ramineni explained that in India, app adoption is one of the highest.“One thing I'm immediately seeing is the use of our mobile app in India, especially because people are having a lot of in-person meetings. And the mobile app has been a big adoption where they're able to just pull out Firefly's hit and record on it. And that's been something we're seeing uniquely,” he said.“We've constantly been increasing beyond Hindi to other languages as well. Today, Firefly supports almost 100 different languages and continues to improve on that aspect. And then, from our own point of view, we’re announcing this gradually but we want to create plant pricing plans specific for India that are more geo-friendly,” Ramineni told TOI.When asked about AI regulation, Ramineni said that the company has different AI policies in different markets.“I want to take a particular example here, which is around call recording consent. It's different in many markets, and we've always taken that position that consent is necessary. It's mandatory in many places, and you should make it explicit,” he said, adding that there may be certain countries that don't have consent-related policy, but we're going to be proactive and do what is the right thing.He explained that the company takes the “highest standard” and follows that. “Be it anywhere. We’ve decided not to set different standards for different countries.”Fireflies.ai is used by over 20 million people and 1 million organisations, including 75% of the Fortune 500. According to the company, it has processed more than 7 billion meeting minutes and integrates with 100+ workplace tools.
Article Summary: Fireflies.ai co-founder and CEO Krish Ramineni: 'Knowledge is fragmented. If you're using Google's AI, it’s only going to work on Google and not on [Microsoft] Teams, or Zoom,’ he told The Times of India tech.

Article Title: No AI in GTA 6 actually means no generative AI, and there is a difference
Article Text:
GTA 6 has no generative AI, but its traffic, pedestrians and police still run on AI (Image via Rockstar Games)

Vice City was built street by street, not prompted into existence

No microtransactions in GTA 6 , but the Ultimate Edition still costs $20 more

Rockstar has confirmed that Grand Theft Auto 6 will launch with no generative AI and no way to spend real money inside the game. Rob Nelson, co-studio head at Rockstar North, gave both answers during a preview visit to the studio's Edinburgh headquarters, speaking to Kinda Funny Games hosts Andy Cortez and Greg Miller. Miller says he put the AI question point-blank. The answer was no.That needs unpacking, because "no AI" and "no generative AI" are not the same sentence. Grand Theft Auto has run on artificial intelligence since the series went 3D. Traffic that reroutes around a crash, pedestrians who react to a drawn weapon, police who coordinate a chase across three blocks: all of that is AI, and all of it is still in GTA 6. What Rockstar is ruling out is the newer stuff, the generative tools that write dialogue, spin up textures or fill a map with machine-made assets.Take-Two chairman Strauss Zelnick said much the same in February, describing Rockstar's worlds as constructed street by street rather than generated. The numbers support that. GTA 6 is reported to carry well over 600,000 animations, against roughly 55,000 in GTA 5 and around 300,000 in Red Dead Redemption 2. That is hand-authored work at a scale that partly explains why this game has taken 13 years.The distinction matters right now because generative AI has become a reputational hazard.Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 and Arc Raiders both took heat from players who spotted machine-generated elements. Rockstar answering the question directly, before launch, closes that argument off early.Cortez asked separately whether players could buy anything with real money in-game and was told there is no monetisation. That is a meaningful commitment for a single-player release, though it comes with an asterisk. The standard edition is $79.99 and the Ultimate Edition is $99.99, and the extra $20 buys cosmetic packs, cars, guns and shops including the Electric Fang tattoo parlour and the Stock 305 clothing store. Rockstar has confirmed standard buyers can upgrade later. Content behind a paywall is still content behind a paywall, just sold once instead of continuously.Rockstar refused to say anything about the next version of GTA Online, which is where Shark Cards have generated real money for over a decade. Nobody expects that model to disappear.The interest is already visible. Sensor Tower estimates pre-orders climbed 436 percent on 27 August, the day the Netflix Extended Look aired, with PlayStation up 606 percent against 127 percent for Xbox.GTA 6 launches 19 November for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S.
Article Summary: GTA 6 launches 19 November for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. Standard edition is $79.99 and the Ultimate Edition is $99.99. Extra $20 buys cosmetic packs, cars, guns and shops including the Electric Fang tattoo parlour and the Stock 305 clothing store.

Article Title: Oracle layoffs: Company leadership may again send the '6 am' email on September 1 that told employees, "We have made the decision to…
Article Text:
September 1: Oracle employees are watching the clock

Oracle employees are refreshing inboxes at 6 am, and swapping dates on Reddit

Why Oracle's RSU vesting calendar is part of the layoff conversation

Oracle has already cut 21,000 jobs in one fiscal year

Oracle revenue is up 17%, which is exactly why these layoffs sting

Oracle employees have spent the last three weeks watching a calendar instead of a dashboard. The company has drawn up plans for another round of job cuts, managers have been asked to submit lists of employees whose roles could be eliminated, and the target is to bring payroll down by September 1, the day Oracle's fiscal second quarter opens. Business Insider first reported the plan, citing people familiar with it and an internal document, and said reductions on some teams could run into double-digit percentages. Oracle declined to comment and has not confirmed anything publicly.Employees now expect the emails to land on the morning of September 1 itself, an expectation that comes from the workforce rather than the company, built on how the last round went. On March 31, thousands of Oracle staff in the US, India, Canada and Mexico woke up at roughly 6 am local time to a note from "Oracle Leadership" that opened with a line about sharing difficult news regarding their position. It said that after careful consideration of Oracle's current business needs, the company had decided to eliminate the role as part of a broader organisational change, and that as a result, today was their last working day.It thanked them for their dedication and impact. Then it told them severance would follow only after they signed termination paperwork, arriving via DocuSign at the Oracle email address they were about to lose access to. There was no HR call and no manager conversation. System access was revoked the same morning.The waiting has produced its own strange rituals. On r/employeesOfOracle, a 52,000-visitor forum that has run a "probable layoff" megathread through August, one employee described checking email at 6 am on the Monday after payday just to confirm he still had a job. Another noted that nothing had landed at 6 am at Oracle's India Development Centre, and reasoned that if the US wave hit first, IDC would follow the next morning, which is roughly how March played out.The rumours have moved around. Some in the thread now expect September 15, pointing to a townhall scheduled that day. Others say after September 24 or 25. Employees in Fusion IDC flagged something odder: several managers at M4 and M6 level took leave from August 24 through September 1, with one poster claiming August 24 was the internal deadline for budget allocation. None of it is confirmed, and the sub's own rules ban unverified layoff rumours, which tells you how much of this is circulating.One longer post tried to impose order on the panic by listing patterns from earlier rounds: the quarterly townhall tends to come before the cuts, rumours start two to three weeks ahead, and there is never a single global date because labour laws differ by region.The other pattern employees keep returning to is stock. Restricted stock units make up a large slice of engineering pay at Oracle, and unvested RSUs are forfeited on exit. A survey of 272 workers cut in March found 27% had stock due to vest within 90 days. One laid-off senior manager said 70% of his compensation sat in RSUs and he was four months from $1 million vesting.That history is why the Reddit thread is full of people counting down to their own vest dates in September, October and November, and asking whether acceleration is negotiable. The consensus answer from those already cut is no. One ex-employee said a group took Oracle to court seeking 2026 RSUs be honoured and lost.This would be a continuation, not a fresh start. Oracle's headcount fell by about 21,000 in the fiscal year ended May 31, roughly 13% of its workforce, taking the company from around 162,000 to about 141,000, of whom roughly 49,000 are in the US. Restructuring costs jumped to $1.8 billion from $374 million a year earlier, a 391% increase.There is not much budget left. Oracle's 10-K, filed June 22, capped the total expected cost of its FY2026 restructuring plan at $2.1 billion. With $1.8 billion booked, that leaves about $300 million of headroom. Cuts on the scale Business Insider describes would either squeeze into that remainder or push Oracle into its second new restructuring plan in three years.Why the $55.7 billion AI data centre bill keeps squeezing Oracle's payrollThe arithmetic is not subtle. Capital expenditure hit $55.7 billion in FY2026, up from $21.2 billion the year before, mostly on data centres for AI customers including OpenAI. Oracle burned $23.7 billion more cash than it generated, raised $43 billion in debt and $5 billion in equity, and expects about $40 billion more this year. Interest expense alone climbed to $4.6 billion from $3.6 billion.TD Cowen estimated in January that cutting 20,000 to 30,000 roles could free up $8-10 billion in incremental free cash flow. Seven months on, that reads less like a forecast and more like a plan.On paper this is not a struggling company. FY2026 revenue rose 17% to $67.4 billion, cloud infrastructure revenue grew 77%, and remaining performance obligations closed the year at $638 billion. Oracle's own annual filing links part of the headcount decline to its adoption of AI, the same technology it is borrowing tens of billions to sell. The stock disagrees, down more than 20% this year, with shareholders suing in January over what Oracle said about the borrowing needed for its $300 billion OpenAI commitment.For employees on this month's lists, the only unknown left is the hour the email arrives.
Article Summary: Oracle employees have spent the last three weeks watching a calendar instead of a dashboard. The company has drawn up plans for another round of job cuts. The target is to bring payroll down by September 1, the day Oracle's fiscal second quarter opens. The waiting has produced its own strange rituals.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Jensen Huang: “Believe in yourself and your abilities. You have the power to…” - a powerful reminder to never underestimate yourself
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Jensen Huang

“Believe in yourself and your abilities. You have the power to make a difference.”

What Jensen Huang’s quote means

What setbacks can teach

Why ability alone is not enough to create change

Confidence still needs work behind it

Lessons learnt from Jensen Huang’s quote

Trust your abilities enough to take the first step

Confidence does not mean certainty

Put your skills into practice

Do not let fear of failure stop you

Keep learning as you move forward

You do not have to achieve something huge to make a difference

Take reasonable risks

Do not underestimate what you can contribute

Let results shape your next move

Build confidence through preparation

There are moments when self-doubt arrives before the work has even begun. A new job, an unfamiliar responsibility or an idea that seems too ambitious can make people question whether they are capable of handling it. Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s co-founder and chief executive, has often spoken about persistence, uncertainty and the need to keep moving through difficult periods. His quote, “Believe in yourself and your abilities. You have the power to make a difference,” takes a straightforward view of confidence. It is not necessarily about feeling certain or expecting success. Instead, it suggests that people need to recognise what they can bring to a situation and be willing to use those abilities. For Huang, whose career has included major changes in computing and technology, that belief has been closely connected with taking risks, learning from mistakes and acting before every answer is known.At its simplest, the message is about having enough confidence to act. That does not mean assuming every decision will be correct or believing that talent alone guarantees success.Self-belief can be quieter than that. It might mean applying for an opportunity despite not meeting every requirement, putting forward an idea that has not been tested or continuing with a difficult project after an early setback.The important part is giving your own abilities a chance to produce something. Confidence and certainty are often treated as though they are interchangeable. They are not. A person can believe they are capable while still knowing that a decision could go wrong. In fact, accepting that possibility can make confidence more useful. It leaves room to listen, learn and change course.For someone building a business, this can mean committing to an idea without knowing exactly where it will lead. In everyday life, it may simply mean taking the next step without having the entire path worked out.Huang has spoken publicly about difficult periods in Nvidia’s history and the importance of responding to failure.A setback can expose weaknesses that success leaves hidden. It can show that an assumption was wrong, that a product needs changing or that a market is moving in another direction. Believing in yourself does not require ignoring those signals. It can mean being confident enough to examine them honestly and try again with better information.That is a different kind of confidence from simply insisting that everything will work.There is a practical point hidden in the final part of Huang’s quote. Having ability is only the starting point. A skilled person who never acts may have less impact than someone with less experience who is prepared to test an idea and improve along the way. Action creates feedback. It shows what works, what fails and what needs to change.This applies well beyond technology or business. A student, employee, artist or entrepreneur can all face the same basic choice: wait until they feel completely ready or make a reasonable attempt and learn from the result. The phrase “make a difference” can sound like it refers only to major achievements. It does not have to. A meaningful contribution can be small. Helping someone solve a problem, improving a process at work, sharing knowledge or creating something useful can all have an effect.The value may not be immediately visible either. Some decisions only show their importance much later. Huang’s words can therefore be read less as a demand to achieve something extraordinary and more as a reminder not to underestimate the usefulness of your own skills.Self-belief cannot replace preparation. Someone may believe they can become a good programmer, manager, engineer or writer, but that belief has to be followed by practice. Skills develop through repetition, mistakes, feedback and experience.Huang’s own career reflects that relationship between confidence and technical ability. His background in engineering gave him a foundation, while decades of working in technology provided opportunities to refine that knowledge.
Article Summary: Jensen Huang’s quote is about having enough confidence to act. Confidence and certainty are often treated as though they are interchangeable. A person can believe they are capable while still knowing that a decision could go wrong. Accepting that possibility can make confidence more useful. A meaningful contribution can be small.

Article Title: As Apple gets a new CEO, here's what fifteen years of Tim Cook did to the company, in numbers
Article Text:
From $108 billion to $416 billion: Tim Cook's 15 years at Apple

Apple was a $108 billion company, it is now a $416 billion one

Three billion iPhones later, the iPhone is still half the business

India had no factory in 2011 and builds a quarter of all iPhones now

China buys less and still makes almost everything

Services went from nothing to Apple's most profitable thing

The Watch and AirPods together outsell the Mac

The $3,499 headset was Cook's one big bet that did not pay

Building its own chip made the Mac a $33.7 billion business again

Regulators have taken $19 billion out of Europe alone

Two years spent on a promise Apple could not keep

$880 million in pay and 0.02 per cent of Apple is what Tim Cook leaves with after 15 years

Tim Cook took over Apple in August 2011, weeks before Steve Jobs died, and hands it to John Ternus tomorrow, September 1, after fifteen years in the job.He took the job as the man who ran the factories, at a moment when nobody believed Apple could survive without the man who imagined the products. Fifteen years later the company is worth thirteen times more, and he leaves it at the top of everything it does. Here is the fifteen years, counted.Apple closed the financial year Cook inherited with $108 billion in revenue and $26 billion in earnings. It closed last year with $416.16 billion and $112 billion in profit, then did $254.9 billion in the first half of this financial year alone.The line was never straight. The first stretch was pure iPhone, peaking when Apple sold 74.5 million of them in the December 2014 quarter and booked $74.6 billion in a single three-month period. Then it stalled. Revenue slipped in 2016, and by the December 2018 quarter iPhone revenue had fallen 15 per cent year on year, mostly on weak China demand.That quarter reshaped the company. While the iPhone fell 15 per cent, everything else grew 19 per cent. Apple stopped publishing unit sales after 2018 and began reporting how many devices were in active use instead, a number that was 1.5 billion in early 2020 and is over 2.5 billion today.The strategy from then on was not to sell more phones. It was to sell more things to the people who already had one.Cook oversaw every iPhone from the 4S to the 17, and Apple shipped 3.1 billion of them on his watch, including 247.8 million in 2025, more than any other manufacturer sold that year.The phone brought in $209.59 billion last financial year, 50.4 per cent of everything Apple made. Fifteen years of building other businesses barely moved that share. It was 52.5 per cent the year before, and roughly the same a decade ago.What did change is where the money comes from inside that number. Unit growth stopped being the lever and price took over. iPhone revenue rose 22 per cent in the June quarter this year to $54.25 billion, and Apple credited Pro models specifically. In India, more than 60 per cent of every phone sold above Rs 50,000 is now an iPhone. The company still rises and falls on one product line.When Cook took the job, India had no Apple store and no Apple factory. It has both today, and the factories carry global weight.Roughly a quarter of the world's iPhones are assembled here, about 55 million units in 2025, up 53 per cent in a year, by Foxconn, Tata Electronics and Pegatron. The entire iPhone 17 line was built in India before launch. Exports crossed $12.8 billion in calendar 2024, and India shipped a record $10 billion worth of iPhones in the first six months of FY26 alone. The iPhone is now the country's single largest export item.Selling took longer than making. The first two stores opened in Mumbai and Delhi in April 2023, and there are six today after Bengaluru, Pune, Noida and Borivali. Apple holds close to 10 per cent of the Indian smartphone market by volume, and revenue here hit a record of about $9 billion in FY25.Greater China brought in $64.4 billion last year, 15.5 per cent of Apple's revenue, down from nearly 19 per cent two years earlier. That is a market Apple has become measurably less dependent on, and demand there has recovered anyway, with $25.5 billion in the December quarter and the best iPhone quarter Apple has ever recorded in that market.The manufacturing side did not move with the sales. About 90 per cent of Apple's suppliers were building at least partly in China or Taiwan before the company stopped publishing that list in 2024. When the US announced global tariffs in April last year, Apple lost $638 billion of market value in three days. India carries a growing share of the load, not the bulk of it, and that gap is what Ternus inherits.The App Store, iCloud, Apple Music, Apple Pay, AppleCare and advertising were a rounding error when Cook took over. Services revenue was $32.7 billion in 2017, $46.3 billion in 2019, $96.2 billion in 2024 and $109.16 billion last year, the first time it crossed $100 billion.Size is not what makes it the most profitable part of Apple. Margin is. Services run at 75.4 per cent gross margin against 36.8 per cent on hardware, so roughly a quarter of Apple's revenue produces close to half its gross profit. Every dollar here is worth about two from a device.The scale underneath it is the installed base. Paid subscriptions crossed 1.5 billion this June. The App Store handled more than $1.4 trillion in developer billings and sales in 2025 and draws over 850 million users a week across 175 countries. This is also the business regulators keep cutting into, which is why every app store ruling gets treated as front-page news.Cook put plenty of new hardware on Apple's shelves. The Apple Watch in 2015, AirPods in 2016, HomePod in 2018, AirTag in 2021 and the Vision Pro in 2024. He also killed the iPod, shut down a decade-long car project in 2024, and moved the Mac to Apple's own chips.Two of those landed, and one of them turned out to be the biggest surprise. Wearables, home and accessories brought in $12.8 billion in 2017, $17.4 billion in 2018 and $24.5 billion in 2019, by which point the segment had already passed the iPad. Last year it did $35.69 billion, ahead of the Mac at $33.7 billion and the iPad at $28 billion, on roughly 80 million AirPods and 33.3 million Watches sold in 2025.Accessories to the iPhone now outsell the computer the company was named for. The segment has also declined three years running, which makes it one of the first problems on Ternus's desk.The Vision Pro arrived in 2024 at $3,499, and Cook talked about it as the device that would eventually do to computing what the iPhone did to the phone. Two years on it has no revenue line of its own, sitting inside that same wearables segment.Apple has since cut jobs across the group that builds it, including people working on device security, audio, testing and the operating system it runs on. The executive who ran the headset and smart glasses division left for OpenAI in June. A rebuilt version is not expected before the end of 2028.Two of Cook's three hardware bets were accessories, priced as an easy second purchase for people who already had an iPhone. The third was meant to become a category in its own right and has not, and that is where Ternus starts.The Mac looks much as it did in 2011. What runs it does not. Dropping Intel for Apple's own silicon changed the cost of every machine the company builds, and the effect shows up across the whole business, not just the Mac.Apple's company-wide gross margin was around 40 per cent when Cook took over. It hit 50.1 per cent in the June quarter this year. That is the single biggest reason profit has grown faster than revenue for most of his tenure.The Mac got a second life out of it too. Revenue in that quarter was a June-quarter record $10.4 billion, up 29 per cent, on the MacBook Neo and MacBook Pro, which makes a category the industry had written off as flat Apple's fastest-growing hardware line right now.Cook's final week in the job brought two new Macs with two new chips for them, and that can very well be the measure of what happened to the Mac under him, at a company that spent years fielding questions about whether it still cared about computers.The bigger Apple got, the more of it ended up in court, and Europe has been the expensive room. The EU ordered Apple to pay $14.4 billion in back taxes over its Irish arrangements in 2016, and competition regulators have levied about $4 billion in antitrust fines since 2011, including €500 million in April 2025 for failing to comply with the Digital Markets Act.The rulings cost more than the fines. Apple has had to allow rival app stores in the EU since March 2024, US developers can link out to their own payment systems at zero commission after the Epic contempt ruling, and take rates have been cut in several markets. Every one of those decisions comes out of the 75 per cent margin business above. The US Department of Justice also sued Apple over smartphone monopoly claims in 2024, and that case is still live.Apple announced Apple Intelligence in mid-2024 and shipped part of it that autumn. The feature it had led with, a Siri that could actually act across your apps, did not arrive. It slipped by nearly two years. Cook removed the executive running AI and reassigned the one running Siri.While that played out, rivals were committing hundreds of billions to data centres and models. Apple spent almost nothing by comparison and never landed a significant AI acquisition either.The answer was announced in January and shown in June at Cook's final developer conference: a rebuilt Siri running on a Google Gemini model, arriving as a standalone app. A company that spent two decades insisting it built its own core technology now pays Google for the intelligence inside its assistant, and that version still is not available across much of Europe because of the DMA standoff.Apple was worth about $350 billion when Cook started and is worth roughly $4.67 trillion today. The shares are up more than 2,000 per cent, over $1 trillion has gone back to shareholders since he began buybacks in 2012, headcount went from about 60,000 to 166,000, and the store count passed 500 across 27 countries.For all of that, Cook was paid $880 million across fifteen years and holds 0.02 per cent of the company he turned into the second most valuable on earth. The figures describe what he actually was. Not a founder and not an inventor, but the best operator the industry has produced, leaving behind 2.5 billion devices in use, the highest margins in Apple's history, and a product line that turns nineteen next year.Ternus gets all of it from tomorrow. What he has to prove is that Apple can still add a number to this list with something new, which Cook tried once and never managed, and his first attempt comes nine days later at an event Apple has called "Surprise and Shine". The surprise is the harder half.
Article Summary: Tim Cook took over Apple in August 2011, weeks before Steve Jobs died. Apple closed the financial year Cook inherited with $108 billion in revenue and $26 billion in earnings. It closed last year with $416.16 billion and $112 billion in profit, then did $254.9 billion in the first half of this financial year alone.

Article Title: OpenClaw that Sam Altman spent billions on and claims to have beaten GTA 6 gets 'largest update in its history'
Article Text:
Streamlined setup and automatic tool detection

Redesigned browser interface and navigation tools

OpenClaw has rolled out OpenClaw 2.0, marking the most extensive software upgrade in the open-source artificial intelligence (AI) agent platform’s history since its debut last year. Announcing the release, the development team playfully referenced Rockstar Games’ upcoming November title launch with the social post, “HA! We beat GTA 6!” According to the company, the version 2.0 overhaul prioritises user accessibility, significantly cutting down initial installation friction while adding multi-user collaboration tools and deeper cross-platform automation.“Today we released by far the largest update in the history of OpenClaw. It was built by 933 contributors, including 569 first-time contributors, and is composed of over 16,000 pull requests,” the company said, adding, “This update touches every part of OpenClaw, including installation, messaging, memory, skills, models, automations, the browser and native apps, plugins, security, and a very long tail of fixes. ”According to the company, OpenClaw 2.0 simplifies initial onboarding by removing cumbersome manual configurations.For example, rather than requiring complex upfront setup, the software automatically discovers existing AI credentials and local frameworks on a device, including API keys, Claude, ChatGPT, Codex logins, and local runners like LM Studio and Ollama.Additionally, users can start interacting with their personal AI agent immediately, finishing secondary configuration settings through conversational prompts. Desktop deployment across Linux, Windows, and macOS has been streamlined, while mobile apps on iOS and Android now feature a simplified permissions and device pairing flow.“Before this update, we had shipped 106 releases in 230 days, most within a day or two of the one before them, so going nearly seven weeks without shipping was not normal for us. The release cadence slowed, but development moved in the opposite direction because our team was growing, and the increased volume and pace of work outgrew both the foundation of OpenClaw and the process we used to ship it, so we reworked both at the same time,” the company added.The primary browser portal has been completely overhauled into a centralised productivity workspace. The new web dashboard launches straight into active dialogues with the user’s AI agent, consolidating approvals, files, system preferences, and chat threads into one unified view. The new navigation features include pinned chat threads, structured session grouping, unified system search, and real-time Markdown rendering.Version 2.0 also expands the platform’s real-world agentic workflow capabilities allowing users to configure autonomous routines that monitor incoming emails, flag urgent communications, and forward push alerts directly through messaging apps like Telegram. The assistant can also pull information across disparate channels, such as locating a retail invoice in an inbox and automatically replying with the requested info over iMessage.

Article Title: Elon Musk warns that humanity faces threats far beyond climate crisis; says: We have about 50 years to take action, else it will be game over on ...
Article Text:
Elon Musk warned that humanity faces threats

‘We have about 50 years’ to act

Climate research cuts

Tesla CEO Elon Musk has cautioned that transitioning to sustainable energy alone may not be enough to protect Earth from long-term climate threats. Recently, Musk suggested that “sentient satellites” launched to Earth-Sun Lagrange points using mass drivers built on the Moon could one day regulate the planet’s temperature. He said such a system could potentially address global warming for up to 1 billion years, envisioning a future where solar-powered AI satellite constellations make fine adjustments to the amount of solar energy reaching Earth.Musk has also warned that humanity faces threats far beyond today’s climate crisis, noting that “extremely severe extinction events happen every 100 million years or so.” He argued that simply switching to sustainable energy will not be sufficient to prevent catastrophic outcomes. “Space satellites to control temperature and massive geo-engineering will be needed or it will be game over,” Musk wrote.While Musk’s vision of space-based geoengineering is long-term, he stressed the urgency of immediate action. “We have about 50 years or so to take action,” he said, pointing to risks for vulnerable coastal populations. His comments come as climate data shows sustained global warming, with Berkeley Earth estimating that 2025 was the third-warmest year on record, at about 1.44°C above the 1850–1900 average.Musk’s warning coincides with concerns about U.S. climate research funding. Earlier this month, the Trump administration announced it would stop supporting the Arctic Report Card, an annual assessment tracking changes in the rapidly warming Arctic. The move adds to a series of actions scaling back climate research, which officials have criticised as alarmist.
Article Summary: Elon Musk warns that humanity faces threats far beyond today’s climate crisis. ‘We have about 50 years or so to take action,’ he said, pointing to risks for vulnerable coastal populations. His comments come as data shows sustained global warming, with 2025 the third-warmest year on record.

Article Title: Anthropic has a warning for Claude users: We have recently seen some ...
Article Text:
What Anthropic told affected users

The malware behind the attacks

How Anthropic is responding

Poll Vote & Share your view Have you ever experienced unauthorized access to an online account? Yes, multiple times Yes, once No, never 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

What Anthropic is telling users to do

AI giant Anthropic has issued a warning to Claude users after discovering that infostealer malware is hijacking active login sessions to access accounts and drain usage. According to a report by Bleeping Computers, the company said that the attackers are stealing authenticated browser sessions from infected computers, enabling them to bypass passwords and two-factor authentication. Anthropic is signing affected users out of Claude, removing saved payment methods, and refunding unauthorised chargesIn an email sent to affected accounts, Anthropic said it recently became aware of a bad actor using common infostealer malware to steal Claude login sessions directly from people's computers, then using those stolen sessions to access accounts and burn through the victims' usage. The email, which was shared publicly on Reddit by one affected user, also gave people a way to recognise the symptom: if a Claude account's usage limits appeared to refill and then mysteriously drain while the account wasn't actively being used, that pattern was likely the cause.The mechanics of the attack make it particularly hard to notice. Infostealer malware can copy an already-authenticated browser session, meaning an attacker doesn't need to go through a normal password or two-factor authentication login process to gain access — they simply reuse a session that's already been verified.Anthropic said its investigation is still ongoing, but that affected computers were most likely already infected with general-purpose infostealer malware unrelated to Claude itself.The company was explicit on this point, stating it has no reason to believe the malware is connected to Claude, was installed through Claude, or relates to anything the user did within the Claude platform.According to Anthropic, this type of malware typically spreads through downloads or malicious apps, and once installed, harvests information stored locally on a device — including browser passwords, login cookies, and credentials tied to a wide range of other apps and services. A user's Claude session was likely just one of many pieces of data swept up in that broader collection process, with attackers only recently beginning to specifically extract and exploit the Claude sessions from what they'd already gathered.In the case shared on Reddit, the affected user confirmed they had downloaded a pirated game shortly before the compromise, offering a likely explanation for how the malware ended up on their system in the first place.Anthropic said it has identified several specific malware families involved in these attacks, including Vidar, LummaC2, StealC, RedLine, and Acreed on Windows systems, along with Atomic Stealer (AMOS) affecting a small number of Mac users.For accounts identified as compromised, Anthropic is taking several protective steps: signing affected users out of Claude, revoking the stolen sessions, removing any saved payment methods from the account, and refunding charges it identifies as unauthorized.However, the company was clear that this response only addresses the symptom, not the underlying cause. Anthropic warned that signing a user out stops the stolen session from being used, but it doesn't remove the malware itself — meaning if the infection is still present on a user's device, their very next login session could be stolen through the exact same method.Anthropic has urged affected users to take basic follow-up security steps beyond what the company can do on its end, including changing their account credentials, revoking any other active sessions tied to their accounts, and thoroughly removing the malware from their infected computers before logging back in.
Article Summary: AI giant Anthropic has issued a warning to Claude users after discovering that infostealer malware is hijacking active login sessions to access accounts and drain usage. Anthropic is signing affected users out of Claude, removing saved payment methods, and refunding unauthorised charges.
